Hi all — thanks for the context. Quick answers and recommended next steps below.

In-transit encryption:
- We enforce TLS 1.2+ for all external traffic and support mTLS for customer-to-service connections if requested.

At-rest encryption:
- Default: AES-256 encryption for all persisted artifacts (models, KV caches, logs) using Redwood-managed envelope keys.
- CMEK: We support customer-managed keys for Hosted (enterprise tiers) and Dedicated environments via AWS KMS/GCP KMS CMEK integrations. For Hosted CMEK, keys can be configured to be in the customer’s AWS account (Redwood uses KMS APIs with restricted grants).
- Private / On-prem: Full support for external key managers and HSMs (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM) via an external key manager connector (EKM) — recommended for customers requiring FIPS-140-2/3 HW-backed key custody.

Key custody and HSM notes:
- Hosted CMEK (keys in customer account): Redwood requires an IAM role/grants to Encrypt/Decrypt operations — we do not export key material. This meets the typical CMEK ask.
- For FIPS/HSM: we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM or customer-owned HSM in Private deployments; lead time depends on networking and cert provisioning (typically 4–6 weeks for Dedicated/Private, 1–2 weeks for hosted enterprise setup if IAM grants are in place).

Audit & logging controls:
- We provide audit logs for admin actions, key usage, and request traces. Logs can be exported to customer S3 or pushed to their SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
- PII redaction: we can configure log scrubbing rules and provide a redaction pipeline for query texts; we can also offer a retention policy enforcement API to delete raw inputs on demand.

Retention & purge:
- Retention policies can be configured per-route. On-demand purge API available for individual records and bulk deletes; we mirror deletion across caches and long-term storage.

Pilot estimate & next steps:
1) Share SOC2 report and architecture diagram (I’ve attached a short implementation plan).
2) Tech deep-dive (30–45m) to review network, IAM grants, and logging integration — I’m available Thursday 10am PT.
3) If we proceed with Hosted+CMEK: expected pilot readiness ~2 weeks after IAM roles/grants and test keys are provided. Dedicated/Private may take 4–6 weeks.

Attachments: kms-implementation-plan.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

Let me know if you want more detail on the grant types we require or a sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet for IAM roles.
